title: Talking about colleagues and the company
grammar: to be — he/she/it is; we/they are; questions and short answers
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a falar de outras pessoas e coisas usando he is, she is, it is, we are e they are, além de fazer perguntas e dar respostas curtas (Is he...? Are they...? Yes, he is.). Isso é essencial para apresentar colegas, descrever departamentos e responder rápido em reuniões e e-mails na Delta Ducon.
intro: In every meeting you talk about other people and other things. 'He is from the São Paulo office.' 'It is an ISO 9001 company.' 'They are on the water team.'
Today we practise he/she/it is and we/they are, and we learn to ask and answer fast: Is she the manager? Yes, she is.
introAudio: This is Ricardo. He is an engineer. She is his manager. They are on the emissions team. Is he from Diadema? Yes, he is. Let us practise together.
vocab: The water team is small. They are five people.
The sales department is on the second floor.
The client is a large steel company.
The visitor is from a cement plant.
The meeting is at nine o'clock.
Delta Ducon is an environmental company.
practice: He is a new member of the emissions ______.
She is the head of the sales ______.
The ______ is a large mining company from Minas Gerais.
Is the ______ from a cement plant? Yes, he is.
The ______ is at ten in the Diadema factory.
They are engineers from the water ______.
We are ready for the ______ with the client.

audio.title: Meet the team
audio.text: This is Carla. She is the project manager. Marcos is here too. He is an engineer from Uberlândia. They are both on the gas treatment team. The client is Brazilian. It is a big steel company. Is the project ready? Yes, it is. We are proud of this work at Delta Ducon.

readAloud: He is an engineer at Delta Ducon.
She is the project manager.
It is an ISO 9001 company.
We are on the water team.
They are visitors from a cement plant.
fill: ___ he from Diadema? Yes, he is.
___ they ready for the meeting? Yes, they are.
The client ___ very happy with the project.
qa: Is he an engineer?
Yes, he is. / No, he is not.
Is she the manager?
Yes, she is. / No, she is not.
Are they on your team?
Yes, they are. / No, they are not.
Is the company from Brazil?
Yes, it is. It is from São Paulo.
Are we ready for the meeting?
Yes, we are ready.

b.label: They are / We are
b.placeholder: They are on the water team.

sentences: He is an engineer at Delta Ducon.
She is the project manager.
It is an ISO 9001 company.
We are on the emissions team.
They are visitors from a cement plant.
Is he from Diadema? Yes, he is.
Are they ready for the meeting? Yes, they are.
The client is very happy with the project.
grammarPoint: he/she/it usam is; we/they usam are. Para perguntar, comece com o verbo: Is he...? Are they...? A resposta curta repete o verbo: Yes, he is. No, they are not. He is an engineer. — Ele é engenheiro. They are on my team. — Eles estão no meu time.
deepDive: Para he, she e it, o verbo é sempre is. Para we, they (e you) é sempre are. Nas perguntas, invertemos: o verbo vem antes do sujeito (Is she...? / Are we...?). Na resposta curta, nunca use a forma completa depois de Yes: diga 'Yes, he is', não 'Yes, he is an engineer' quando quiser ser breve.
examples: We are on the water team.
Nós estamos na equipe de água.
mistakes: Antes de profissão no singular, use a/an.
Na resposta curta, repita o verbo certo: he is.
A forma negativa é is not.
quick: ___ she the manager? Yes, she is.

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now talk about your whole team in English — a real step toward leading a meeting with confidence.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você consegue falar de toda a sua equipe em inglês — um passo real rumo a conduzir uma reunião com confiança.

title: Around the office: a, an, the and plurals
grammar: Articles a / an / the + plural nouns (regular plurals)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a usar os artigos a, an e the e a formar o plural regular dos substantivos (adicionando -s). Assim você fala com naturalidade sobre objetos, departamentos e pessoas do escritório da Delta Ducon, em e-mails e conversas do dia a dia.
intro: The office is full of things and people: a desk, an engineer, the manager, three factories, many clients.
Today we learn when to say a, an or the, and how to make plurals. Small words, big difference in every e-mail.
introAudio: This is a desk. This is an engineer. The manager is over there. We have three factories and many clients. Let us learn a, an, the and plurals together.
vocab: I am writing a report about the new project.
She sends an email to the client every morning.
The office in São Paulo is our head office.
We have three projects with steel companies.
Please sign the documents for the client.
practice: I am writing a ______ about the water treatment plant.
She sends an ______ to the client every morning.
The head ______ is in São Paulo.
We have three ______ with cement companies.
Please sign the ______ before the meeting.
The factory in Diadema has many ______.
This is an important ______ for the ISO audit.
The ______ from the sales team is very clear.

audio.title: A day at the office
audio.text: Delta Ducon is a company with three factories. We have an office in São Paulo and many clients. Every day the engineers write reports and send emails. The managers read the documents and plan the projects. It is a busy place, but the teams are strong and the work is important for the environment.

readAloud: This is a report about the new project.
She sends an email to the client.
The manager is in the office.
We have three factories in Brazil.
The engineers write many reports.
fill: This is ___ report for the client.
___ office in São Paulo is big.
We have three ___ with steel companies.
I read ___ reports before the meeting.
qa: Is this a report or an email?
It is a report.
Where is the office?
The office is in São Paulo.
How many projects do you have?
We have three projects.
Are there many machines in the factory?
Yes, there are many machines.
Who reads the documents?
The managers read the documents.

a.label: a / an + singular
a.placeholder: This is a report for the client.

sentences: This is a report about the new project.
She is an engineer at Delta Ducon.
The office in São Paulo is our head office.
We have three factories in Brazil.
The engineers write many reports.
Please sign the documents before the meeting.
The factory has many machines.
She sends an email to the client every morning.
grammarPoint: Use a antes de som de consoante (a report) e an antes de som de vogal (an email, an engineer). Use the para algo específico ou já conhecido (the office). O plural regular adiciona -s: report → reports, machine → machines. This is a project. — Isto é um projeto. The engineers write reports. — Os engenheiros escrevem relatórios.
deepDive: a/an aparecem só com substantivos no singular e contáveis; the serve para singular e plural, quando falamos de algo específico. No plural regular, basta acrescentar -s. Palavras terminadas em -y trocam por -ies (company → companies) e algumas em -o/-ch/-s ganham -es, mas o padrão principal é só -s.
examples: The office is in São Paulo.
O escritório fica em São Paulo.
The factories are in São Paulo and Minas Gerais.
As fábricas ficam em São Paulo e em Minas Gerais.
mistakes: Antes de som de vogal, use an.
Antes de som de consoante, use a.
Email começa com som de vogal: an email.

celebrate.en: Excellent work. These small words are everywhere in professional English — mastering them makes your emails sound clear and correct.
celebrate.pt: Excelente trabalho. Essas palavrinhas estão em todo lugar no inglês profissional — dominá-las deixa seus e-mails claros e corretos.

title: In the office: there is, there are, this and that
grammar: there is / there are + this / that / these / those
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a dizer o que existe no ambiente com there is e there are, e a apontar coisas com this, that, these e those. Isso ajuda você a descrever o escritório, a fábrica e uma sala de reunião, e a se referir a documentos e objetos perto ou longe de você na Delta Ducon.
intro: Look around the office. There is a meeting room on the left. There are two engineers at that desk. This is my report; those are the client's documents.
Today we learn there is / there are and this / that / these / those — the words we use to describe a place and point to things.
introAudio: There is a meeting room here. There are three factories at Delta Ducon. This is my desk, and that is the manager's office. Let us describe our workplace together.
vocab: There is a meeting room on the second floor.
There are ten chairs in the meeting room.
This table is for the client meeting.
There is a big window near my desk.
The sales team is on that floor.
There are three plants across Brazil.
practice: There is a meeting ______ on the second floor.
There are ten ______ around the table.
This ______ is for the client meeting.
There is a big ______ near my desk.
The sales team is on that ______.
There are three ______ in São Paulo and Minas Gerais.
Is there a water treatment ______ in Uberlândia? Yes, there is.

audio.title: A tour of the office
audio.text: Welcome to Delta Ducon. There is a reception here, and there are two meeting rooms on this floor. This is the engineering team, and those are the desks of the sales department. There is a big window with a view of the city. There are many projects on the wall. This is a good place to work.

readAloud: There is a meeting room on this floor.
There are three factories in Brazil.
This is my desk.
That is the manager's office.
Those documents are for the client.
fill: ___ a meeting room on this floor.
___ is the manager's office over there.
___ documents on my desk are for you.
___ documents on that desk are for the client.
___ a big window near my desk.
qa: Is there a meeting room here?
Yes, there is. It is on this floor.
How many factories are there?
There are three factories in Brazil.
What is this?
This is a report for the client.
What are those?
Those are the documents for the ISO audit.
Are there chairs for the visitors?
Yes, there are chairs for the visitors.

a.label: There is / There are
a.placeholder: There are three factories in Brazil.

sentences: There is a meeting room on this floor.
There are three factories in Brazil.
This is my desk.
That is the manager's office.
These documents are for you.
Those chairs are for the visitors.
There are two engineers on the water team.
Is there a plant in Uberlândia? Yes, there is.
grammarPoint: Use there is para um (singular): There is a room. Use there are para dois ou mais (plural): There are three plants. Para apontar, use this (perto, singular), these (perto, plural), that (longe, singular), those (longe, plural). This is my desk. — Esta é a minha mesa. Those are the client's documents. — Aqueles são os documentos do cliente.
deepDive: there is/there are dizem o que existe num lugar; combine there is com singular e there are com plural. this/these apontam para o que está perto de você; that/those para o que está longe. Lembre-se: this e that são singular; these e those são plural.
examples: There is a meeting room here.
Há uma sala de reunião aqui.
There are three factories in Brazil.
Aquele é o escritório do gerente.
Those chairs are for the visitors.
Aquelas cadeiras são para os visitantes.
There is a window near my desk.
Há uma janela perto da minha mesa.
There are ten chairs in the room.
Is there a plant in Uberlândia?
mistakes: No plural perto de você, use these.
Para dizer que existe algo, use there is.
quick: ___ is the manager's office over there.

celebrate.en: Great progress. You can now describe any room, office or factory in English — a skill you will use every time you welcome a visitor.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo progresso. Agora você consegue descrever qualquer sala, escritório ou fábrica em inglês — uma habilidade que vai usar sempre que receber um visitante.

title: Whose is it? My, your and the possessive 's
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a dizer de quem é algo usando os adjetivos possessivos my, your, his, her, our e their, além do possessivo com 's (Ana's report, the client's project). Isso ajuda você a organizar tarefas, e-mails e responsabilidades entre colegas e departamentos da Delta Ducon.
intro: Whose report is this? It is my report. That is Ana's desk, and this is the client's project.
Today we learn possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, our, their) and the possessive 's — the words that say who owns what at work.
introAudio: This is my desk and that is her office. Ana's report is ready, and the client's project is on time. Let us learn how to say who owns what at Delta Ducon.
vocab: My boss leads the emissions department.
This task is on your list for today.
The client's schedule is very tight.
Our goal is to protect the environment.
Their team works at the Diadema factory.
practice: This ______ is on your list for today.
The client's ______ is very tight this month.
Our ______ is to protect the environment.
Their ______ works at the Diadema factory.
Ana's ______ for the audit is almost ready.
His ______ is the head of the water division.

audio.title: Whose project is this?
audio.text: This is our team at Delta Ducon. My name is Paulo, and this is my report. Ana is our engineer; her project is the water treatment plant. The client's schedule is tight, but their goal is clear. Our company's mission is to protect the environment, and we are proud of our work.

readAloud: This is my report.
Her project is the water treatment plant.
The client's schedule is tight.
Our mission is to protect the environment.
Ana's desk is next to mine.
fill: He is an engineer. ___ project is the new plant. (dele)
She is the manager. ___ team is strong. (dela)
We are a team. ___ goal is clear. (nosso)
They are engineers. ___ factory is in Diadema. (deles)
qa: Whose report is this?
It is my report.
Is this your desk?
Yes, it is my desk. / No, it is her desk.
What is Delta Ducon's mission?
Its mission is to protect the environment.
Whose project is the water treatment plant?
It is her project.
What is your team's goal?
Our goal is to deliver the project on time.
sentences: This is my report.
Her project is the water treatment plant.
The client's schedule is tight.
Our mission is to protect the environment.
Their team works at the Diadema factory.
Ana's desk is next to mine.
His boss is the head of the water division.
Delta Ducon's goal is a cleaner industry.
grammarPoint: Os adjetivos possessivos vêm antes do substantivo: my, your, his, her, our, their (my report, her project). O possessivo 's diz de quem é algo com nomes de pessoas ou empresas: Ana's report (o relatório da Ana), the client's schedule (o cronograma do cliente). This is my report. — Este é o meu relatório. Ana's project is ready. — O projeto da Ana está pronto.
deepDive: Use my/your/his/her/our/their sempre seguido de um substantivo, sem apóstrofo. Use 's no fim de um nome para indicar posse: the manager's office. Cuidado para não confundir his (dele) com her (dela), e their (deles/delas, possessivo) com there (lá) e they're (they are).
examples: His project is the new plant.
O projeto dele é a nova planta.
A equipe dela é muito forte.
A fábrica deles fica em Diadema.
O relatório da Ana está pronto.
O cronograma do cliente está apertado.
A meta da Delta Ducon é clara.
The manager's office is on this floor.
O escritório do gerente fica neste andar.
mistakes: Antes do substantivo, use my, não me.
Carlos is here; her project is new.
Carlos is here; his project is new.
Use his para ele e her para ela; não troque.
Com nomes de pessoas, use 's em vez de of.
their é posse; they are (they're) é o verbo.
our já é possessivo; não leva 's.

celebrate.en: Outstanding. You can now say who owns what and organise work clearly in English — exactly what a strong professional does every day.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Agora você consegue dizer de quem é cada coisa e organizar o trabalho com clareza em inglês — exatamente o que um bom profissional faz todo dia.
